# Bayesian model specifications

For $\mathcal{N}(m,v)$, the second argument denotes variance. Half-normal distributions are specified by their scale parameters.

## Unconstrained normal population model

$$
\begin{aligned}
y_{ij}\mid\theta_i
&\sim \mathcal{N}(\theta_i,\sigma_\epsilon^2),\\
\theta_i
&\sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_\theta,\sigma_\theta^2),\\
\log\mu_\theta
&\sim \mathcal{N}(0.5,1^2),\\
z
&\sim \mathcal{N}\!\left(-\frac23,\left(\frac23\right)^2\right),\\
p&=\frac{\Phi(z)}{2},\\
\sigma_\theta
&=-\frac{\mu_\theta}{\Phi^{-1}(p)},\\
\pi(\sigma_\epsilon)
&\propto\sigma_\epsilon^{-2},
\qquad \sigma_\epsilon>0.
\end{aligned}
$$

## Approximate dominance model

The specification was identical to the unconstrained model except that:

$$
z\sim\mathcal{N}(-3.5,0.5^2).
$$

This concentrated prior probability on small negative-effect proportions.

## Strictly positive log-normal population model

$$
\begin{aligned}
y_{ij}\mid\theta_i
&\sim\mathcal{N}(\theta_i,\sigma_\epsilon^2),\\
\log\theta_i
&\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu_{\log},\sigma_{\log}^2),\\
\mu_{\log}
&\sim\mathcal{N}(0.5,1^2),\\
\sigma_{\log}
&\sim\operatorname{HalfNormal}(1),\\
\sigma_\epsilon
&\sim\operatorname{HalfNormal}(5),\\
P(\theta_i<0)&=0.
\end{aligned}
$$

Population summaries on the original spatial scale were derived as:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mu_\theta
&=\exp\!\left(\mu_{\log}+\frac{\sigma_{\log}^2}{2}\right),\\
\sigma_\theta
&=\sqrt{
\left[\exp(\sigma_{\log}^2)-1\right]
\exp(2\mu_{\log}+\sigma_{\log}^2)
}.
\end{aligned}
$$
